# Pranjul Rathour

> GenAI engineering, hackathons and campus talks, answered from experience. Written by Pranjul Rathour, GenAI engineer in India (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com). Each page answers real search questions about one topic, cites primary sources, and draws on production systems he shipped (RAG.NextUpgrad, FineTune Studio, DocuLens AI, FaceVision, OCR & Speech Workspace) and three hackathon first prizes.

- [About Pranjul Rathour](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/about/): bio, experience, awards, sessions delivered
- [Contact](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/contact/): email and every profile
- [Invite Pranjul to your campus](https://pranjulrathour.scult.in/invite): talks, workshops, hackathon judging and mentoring; book at https://pranjulrathour.scult.in/book
- [FAQ](https://pranjulrathour.scult.in/faq): inviting, hiring, booking and about, answered; full text at https://pranjulrathour.scult.in/llms-full.txt

## Travel, stay and fees for campus sessions

For campus sessions the inviting institution covers the visit end to end: travel (a First AC train ticket for journeys up to five hours, a flight for anything longer), accommodation, meals, and pickup and drop. The honorarium and workshop fees are negotiable on WhatsApp or on the call; requests are welcome from institutions that can cover the visit this way. Details: https://pranjulrathour.scult.in/invite#travel

## RAG & retrieval

Retrieval-augmented generation, vector search and grounded answers, from a production platform.

- [What is machine learning, and what is it actually used for? The three types, how it differs from AI and deep learning, and real applications](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/what-is-machine-learning/): Machine learning is software that improves at a task from data instead of following rules a programmer wrote by hand. Supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning explained plainly, how ML relates to AI and deep learning, and where it is genuinely used today, from spam filters to the models behind modern generative AI.
- [What is a vector database? How vector search works, when you need one, and FAISS vs pgvector vs Qdrant vs Pinecone](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/what-is-a-vector-database/): A vector database stores embeddings and finds the nearest ones fast. How vector search and ANN indexes work, when a library or Postgres is enough, and how to choose between FAISS, pgvector, Qdrant, Chroma, Weaviate, Pinecone and Milvus.
- [What is an LLM? Large language models explained: tokens, context windows, parameters, open vs closed models, and what they cost to run](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/what-is-an-llm/): A large language model predicts the next token, and everything else follows from that. How LLMs are trained, what parameters, tokens and context windows mean, how GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama and Mistral differ, what hallucination is, how to run one locally, and how to reason about cost. Written from shipping LLM products.
- [Does agentic AI use RAG? RAG vs agents, MCP, ChatGPT, design tips and LlamaIndex](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/agentic-ai-and-rag/): Whether agentic AI uses RAG, RAG vs agentic AI, ChatGPT as agentic RAG, RAG vs MCP, whether agentic RAG is worth it, design tips and LlamaIndex.
- [AI hallucination examples: what it means, why it happens, and real cases](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/ai-hallucination-examples/): What hallucination means in generative AI, why it is called that and why it happens, real examples from ChatGPT, LLMs and the news, and medical hallucinations.
- [What is AI hallucination? Why LLMs hallucinate and how to prevent it](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/ai-hallucination-explained/): AI hallucination is when a model states something false as fact. Why LLMs hallucinate, how to test for it, and how to reduce it in ChatGPT and RAG systems.
- [Best local LLM for coding: agentic models, 8 to 24 GB VRAM, 16 GB RAM, leaderboards](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/best-local-llm-coding-vram/): The best local LLMs for coding and agentic coding by VRAM tier, running on 16 GB of RAM, coding leaderboards, and why local agents stall mid-task.
- [Which Ollama model is best for coding? Local, agentic, tools, reasoning and embeddings](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/best-ollama-model-for-coding/): The best Ollama models for coding, local and agentic coding, cloud models, tool support, reasoning, image generation, embeddings, reranking, and training.
- [Best open source LLMs now: examples, coding, function calling, embeddings, rerankers](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/best-open-source-llms-embeddings-rerankers/): Current best open LLMs, examples, function calling, coding, rerankers, embeddings, vector search, observability, and open weight vs open source.
- [Text embedding models: how they are trained, uses, best for RAG and Ollama, OpenAI facts](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/best-text-embedding-models/): How embedding models are trained, uses, best models for 2026, RAG and Ollama, OpenAI licensing and languages, metrics, and image-text embeddings.
- [BM25 explained: Best Matching 25 meaning, origin, formula, TF-IDF, BM25F, SPLADE, BM42](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/bm25-explained-formula-vs-tfidf/): What BM25 means, why it is called BM25, when it was created, how it is calculated, how it differs from TF-IDF, BM25F, SPLADE and BM42, and its scores.
- [What is a BM25 score? Ranking, calculation, negatives, normalisation, indexes, and cosine](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/bm25-score-explained/): What BM25 ranking and scores are, calculating them by hand, negative scores, normalising, BM25 indexes, Gensim, BM25 vs cosine similarity, and legitimacy.

Chat with PDF tools, upload limits, and exporting chats to PDF](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-pdf-chat-with-pdf/): What chat-with-PDF tools are and how they work, building one, ChatGPT PDF upload problems and limits, making PDFs, and exporting ChatGPT or WhatsApp chats.
- [Chroma vs ChromaDB: what Chroma does in Python, examples and common errors](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chroma-vector-database-python/): Chroma, or ChromaDB, is an open-source vector database. Using it in Python, examples, avoiding re-embedding, in-memory storage and a common crash.
- [What is the chunking method? Memory, English language chunks, NLP, and division](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chunking-method-explained/): What chunking means in memory, who came up with it, examples, why it helps memory, chunking in English, chunking vs tokenization, and the division method.

## Blog

Build logs, hackathon stories and career notes (286 articles, newest first; index at https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/, machine-readable at https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/posts.json).

- [From mentee to mentor to judge: a natural progression, not a hierarchy](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/from-mentee-to-mentor-to-judge-a-natural-progression/): The path from being mentored, to mentoring others, to judging their work isn't a ladder to climb — it's a set of roles the same person can hold at once, at any stage.
- [Running a judges-only debrief right after the event: the fifteen minutes organisers skip](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/running-a-judges-only-debrief-after-the-event/): A short debrief among judges, right after results are decided, surfaces process improvements while they're still fresh — and is skipped far more often than it should be.
- [Speaking about AI to non-engineering college audiences: what actually needs to change](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/speaking-to-non-engineering-college-audiences/): A talk built for CS students falls flat with commerce or arts students. What genuinely needs adjusting, and what stays honest and useful either way.
- [What I wish someone had told me before my first hackathon judging gig](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/what-i-wish-organisers-told-me-before-my-first-judging-gig/): First-time judging comes with a few surprises nobody warns you about — the pace, the fatigue, the awkward moments. A few things worth knowing in advance.
- [Building a personal brand as a campus speaker, without it feeling like self-promotion](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/building-a-personal-brand-as-a-campus-speaker/): Consistent positioning — a clear niche, a recognisable set of talks — helps organisers know exactly what to book you for. How to do this without it feeling hollow.
- [Judging a hackathon where you're also personally sponsoring a prize](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/judging-a-hackathon-you-also-sponsored-prizes-for/): Occasionally a judge is also the one putting up a prize from their own pocket or company. How to keep that arrangement transparent and fair to every team.
- [How organisers should train first-time judges before the event, not during it](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/how-hackathon-organisers-train-new-judges/): A briefing on event day is necessary but not sufficient. What organisers can do beforehand to prepare judges who've never done this before.
- [Mentoring through open source: a different channel from talks and workshops](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/mentoring-through-open-source-instead-of-talks/): Reviewing pull requests and answering issues on a public repo is its own form of mentorship — quieter, asynchronous, and reaching people a talk never would.
- [Why my RAG platform says "I don't know" — building RAG.NextUpgrad](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/rag-nextupgrad-confidence-gate/): Inside RAG.NextUpgrad: hybrid dense + BM25 retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, and the confidence gate that refuses to answer on weak evidence.
- [Speaking at international student conferences remotely: what changes across borders](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/speaking-at-international-student-conferences-remotely/): A remote talk to students in another country adds time zones, cultural context and sometimes language considerations on top of the usual remote-speaking mechanics.
- [Hackathon sponsors and judging: staying neutral when a sponsor's tech is on the table](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/sponsor-relations-for-hackathon-judges-staying-neutral/): Sponsor prizes for 'best use of X API' create a real conflict-of-interest question for judges. How to keep sponsor-track judging fair and clearly separated.
- [Fine-tuning a 1.7B model at 3.2 GB VRAM — building FineTune Studio](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/finetune-studio-qlora-on-a-budget/): How FineTune Studio runs QLoRA fine-tuning end to end in a browser, on hardware a student can actually afford, with honest base-vs-tuned evaluation.
- [A year of shipping: SCULT INDIA, TechVerse Enclave, and NextUpgrad](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/a-year-of-shipping/): Looking back at a year that included co-founding a studio, growing a 500-member community, and shipping five production AI apps solo.
- [Handling long-running AI agents: timeouts, checkpoints and partial progress](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/handling-long-running-ai-agents-timeouts-and-checkpoints/): An agentic task that runs for minutes needs a different failure model than a single API call. Timeouts, checkpointing and resuming partial work, done right.
- [Face recognition that never uploads a face — building FaceVision](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/facevision-privacy-first-recognition/): FaceVision runs detection, recognition and liveness checks entirely in the browser with ONNX Runtime Web. The backend never sees an image, only vectors.
- [Building an internal AI tool for your own team: a lower-stakes way to ship something real](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/building-an-internal-tool-with-ai-for-your-own-team/): An internal tool has real users (your teammates) without the stakes of a public product. A genuinely good way to practice the full build-to-deploy loop.
- [Versioning prompts like you version code: a simple system that pays off fast](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/versioning-prompts-like-you-version-code/): A prompt edited directly in the codebase with no history becomes impossible to debug when quality regresses. Simple prompt versioning fixes this cheaply.
- [Reading an invoice like an auditor — building DocuLens AI](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/doculens-ai-deterministic-document-intelligence/): DocuLens AI extracts, compares and compliance-checks business documents with schema-validated, deterministic scoring — not a free-text LLM summary.
- [Graceful degradation: what your app should do when the LLM provider is down](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/graceful-degradation-when-the-llm-provider-is-down/): Every provider has occasional outages. An app with no fallback plan goes fully dark; one designed for degradation keeps working in a reduced but honest way.
- [Setting up cost alerts for AI APIs before the bill surprises you](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/cost-alerts-for-ai-apis-before-the-bill-surprises-you/): A rate limit stops a runaway loop from crashing your app. A cost alert stops it from crashing your budget. Both are needed, and most student projects only build the first.
- [Every page and every word, searchable — building the OCR & Speech Workspace](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/ocr-speech-workspace-mistral/): A Mistral-powered workspace for page-batched PDF OCR, live speech-to-text, and document-scoped chat with citations.
- [Webhooks and async callbacks for AI pipelines: notifying instead of polling](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/webhooks-and-async-callbacks-for-ai-pipelines/): Polling a job-status endpoint every few seconds wastes resources on both sides. A webhook-based callback pattern is often the better fit for slow AI tasks.
- [Building a support-ticket triage system with an LLM: a project walkthrough](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/building-a-support-ticket-triage-system/): Classifying, prioritising and routing incoming support tickets is a genuinely useful, well-scoped AI project with a clear before-and-after metric.
- [Shipping side projects that survive demo day](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/shipping-side-projects-that-survive-demo-day/): Why most student projects die the day after they are shown, and the handful of habits that keep one alive: a real user, a deploy that stays up, a changelog, monthly maintenance, and knowing when to archive well.
- [Handling personal data (PII) in LLM applications without it leaking where it shouldn't](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/handling-pii-in-llm-applications/): Sending user PII to a third-party LLM API, logging it in plaintext, or letting it leak into a training set are three distinct risks. What to actually do about each.
- [A/B testing an AI feature: what to actually measure beyond click-through rate](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/ab-testing-an-ai-feature-what-to-measure/): Standard A/B testing metrics don't capture whether an AI answer was actually correct or useful. What metrics matter specifically for testing AI feature changes.
- [Agentic AI patterns: tools, memory and guardrails without the hype](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/agentic-ai-patterns-tools-memory-guardrails/): What an 'agent' is in production terms — a loop with tools — and the patterns that make one safe to ship: least-privilege tools, retrieved text as data, bounded loops, inspectable memory and a pause path.
- [Feature flags for AI features: rolling out a new model or prompt safely](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/feature-flags-for-ai-features-safe-rollouts/): Shipping a new prompt or model version to everyone at once is how a regression reaches every user simultaneously. Feature flags let you roll out gradually and roll back fast.
- [Secrets management for student projects: never commit an API key again](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/secrets-management-student-projects/): The habits that keep keys out of repositories and demos: ignored environment files, committed example files, server-side keys only, rotation after a leak, and what to do in the first ten minutes if one gets out.
- [Generating alt text with vision AI: a genuinely useful accessibility application](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/accessibility-and-vision-ai-alt-text-generation/): Auto-generating image alt text with a vision-language model is one of the more directly useful, low-risk applications of the technology. What makes a generated alt text good.
- [Video summarization with vision-language models: what's actually feasible today](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/video-summarization-with-vision-language-models/): Full automatic video summarization is an active research area. A realistic, achievable version of it using frame sampling plus a vision-language model.
- [Controlling LLM costs: token budgets, caching and cheaper routing](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/llm-cost-control-token-budgets/): How to keep an AI product's bill predictable: per-request context caps, embedding and response caches, routing simple requests to small models, fallback spend limits, and the dashboard that shows cost per feature.
- [Building a plant or object identifier app: a well-scoped vision project](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/building-a-plant-or-object-identifier-app/): A photo-to-identification app is visual, has a clear success metric, and is achievable with a pretrained model plus a well-curated reference dataset.

- [Vision API costs: cloud vision APIs vs self-hosting a model, a real comparison](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/vision-api-costs-cloud-vs-self-hosted/): Per-image API pricing looks cheap at low volume and expensive fast. Near-duplicates — the same example paraphrased — quietly bias a fine-tune and are far more common than people expect.

A context-budget framework](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/context-window-budget-how-much-retrieved-text-to-include/): More context isn't always better — past a point, extra chunks dilute attention and cost more without improving the answer. Standard embedding models handle this unevenly — what to test before trusting them.

- [Prompt injection vs memory poisoning: a practical guide for builders](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/prompt-injection-vs-memory-poisoning/): Prompt injection resets when a chat ends. Memory poisoning doesn't. If your agent has memory, it needs a different threat model.
- [Multi-tenant RAG: making sure one customer never sees another customer's documents](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/multi-tenant-rag-isolating-data-between-customers/): A shared vector index serving multiple customers needs strict isolation, not just a metadata filter that a bug could silently bypass. - [Document AI for invoices: schema-first extraction that auditors can trust](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/document-ai-invoices-extraction-schema/): Why free-form 'AI reads your invoice' fails, and how schema-validated extraction with deterministic scoring, field-level confidence and comparison against source documents makes document intelligence defensible.
- [The RAG security hole nobody checks: prompt injection hiding inside retrieved documents](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/rag-security-prompt-injection-via-retrieved-documents/): A malicious instruction embedded in a document your RAG system retrieves can hijack the model's behaviour. - [Synthetic data for fine-tuning: when it works and when it teaches the model your own mistakes](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/synthetic-data-for-fine-tuning-when-it-works/): Generating training examples with a bigger model can fill a data gap fast, or quietly bake in that model's biases and errors. How to tell which you're getting.
- [Self-hosted vs managed vector search: what actually changes at student-project scale](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/self-hosted-vs-managed-vector-search/): pgvector on a free Postgres instance vs a managed vector database — the real trade-offs for a project with under a million vectors, not an enterprise deployment.
- [RAG observability: the five things worth logging (and the ten that aren't)](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/rag-observability-what-to-log/): Logging everything drowns the one signal that matters. A short list of what to actually capture from a production retrieval pipeline, and why.
- [The RAG question nobody plans for: 'what if it's just not in the documents?'](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/handling-out-of-scope-questions-in-rag/): A confidence gate catches weak matches, but out-of-scope questions need a different check: does the retrieved context even address the question's topic at all?
- [RAG over a SQL database: why text-to-SQL is a different problem](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/rag-with-sql-databases-text-to-sql-patterns/): Vector search doesn't help when the answer is 'run this aggregate query'. A practical pattern for letting an LLM answer questions against a real database safely.
- [Multi-hop questions break single-pass RAG. Here's the pattern that fixes it](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/multi-hop-questions-in-rag-systems/): 'Who won the hackathon the year after X joined?' needs two retrieval steps, not one. A simple decompose-then-retrieve pattern for multi-hop questions.
- [Where a RAG request's latency actually goes (it isn't the LLM call)](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/rag-latency-budget-where-time-goes/): Profiling a real RAG endpoint end to end: embedding, vector search, reranking, prompt assembly and generation each take a slice — and the slowest part surprises most people.
- [Teaching AI-powered software development to first-year engineers](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/ai-powered-software-development-session/): Inside the VSICS session where I mapped how AI now touches every stage of the software lifecycle, from requirements to maintenance.
- [Semantic caching for RAG: when it saves money and when it lies to users](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/semantic-cache-for-rag-when-it-helps/): Caching by exact string match misses near-duplicate questions; semantic caching catches them, but a badly-tuned similarity threshold serves stale, wrong answers.
- [RAG for PDFs with tables and images: what breaks and how to fix it](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/rag-for-pdfs-with-tables-and-images/): Plain-text chunking destroys tables and ignores images. A practical pipeline for PDFs that actually contain the data your users are asking about.
- [Metadata filtering in RAG: the retrieval fix nobody mentions first](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/metadata-filtering-in-rag-pipelines/): Before you touch embeddings or rerankers, filter by metadata — date, source, document type. It is the cheapest accuracy gain in a retrieval pipeline.
- [I ran the chunk-size experiment so you don't have to: what actually changed](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/rag-chunk-size-experiments-what-actually-works/): Testing 128, 256, 512 and 1024-token chunks on the same retrieval pipeline, with the same eval set, to see which size actually moved recall and answer quality.
- [What a college debate stage taught me about arguing a position I don't hold](https://pranjulrathour.github.io/blog/insight-talk-show-arguing-against-nationalism/): At INSIGHT — The Talk Show, VSICS, I argued against the motion on nationalism and policy. It's a soft-skill exercise every engineer should try.
